newsitem.title: BELGIUM: KIDNAPPER OF FORMER BELGIAN PM FOUND GUILTY.
newsitem.headline: KIDNAPPER OF FORMER BELGIAN PM FOUND GUILTY.

text.p: Basri Bajrami, dubbed the Houdini of Belgian crime for the number of times he escaped from jail, was found guilty on Thursday on multiple counts of armed robbery and the kidnapping of a former prime minister.

The swarthy Macedonian was the last member at large of the Haemers gang, which wrought havoc across Belgium in the 1980s, ending with the abduction and ransoming of former Belgian Prime Minister Paul Vanden Boeynants.
Bajrami broke out of a Belgian prison in 1993 in an escape that would have had film directors drooling.
He last appeared in a Belgian court in April 1993, shortly before his escape. The case had to be adjourned because such was the fear of the Haemers Gang that not enough jurors could be found.
During the trial that began five weeks ago, the jury had to sift through evidence contained in than 134 folders, each with more than 1,000 pages.
Bajrami has already been tried and sentenced to death in absentia on charges related to his membership of the gang.
The death penalty was erased from the statute books in June. Under Belgian law a trial had to be held once Bajrami, 41, was back in jail.
The Haemers Gang's career culminated in the kidnapping in January 1989 of Vanden Boeynants, who was released after a month for a ransom reputed to have been more than $1.5 million.
The leader of the gang, Patrick Haemers, was caught in Brazil in May 1989 and extradited to Belgium. He hanged himself in prison in 1993.
Bajrami's notoriety was enhanced by his dramatic escape from a Brussels jail in 1993, recorded by news cameras filming a prison riot.
A hostage was spreadeagled across the windshield of the escape car, his head through the sunroof, and the gangster's pistol jammed in his mouth.
Bajrami was extradited to Belgium two years later from his native Macedonia. REUTER
